rgb: The view shows the corner of an indoor room where two beige walls meet, with floor-to-ceiling curtains next to a glass door approximately 2 to 3 metres away on the right. In the first frame, a small dark table in the corner sits about 1.5 to 2 metres from the camera wearer and supports a white router, a dark telephone, and a white cord. A white highchair with dark padding is directly ahead of and below the wearer at roughly 0.5 to 0.8 metres—comfortably within arm's reach—with a bottle on its tray and a baby wearing a red top seated inside. Initially, the baby faces the camera wearer and looks upward, while the highchair backrest partly blocks the corner table. From frames 1 through 3, the highchair rotates clockwise as the wearer advances and passes around its right side toward the corner. During this movement, the baby turns their head and upper torso toward the backrest and away from the wearer, and the fully visible corner table moves to the right of the image at a distance of about 1 to 1.5 metres. In frame 4, the wearer is immediately behind the highchair and looks sharply downward; the corner table is around 1 metre ahead, the wearer's bare right foot appears at the lower right, and nearly all of the tray and baby fall outside the bottom-left edge, leaving only the baby's hands holding the top of the backrest visible. By frame 5, the wearer has turned left toward the highchair's side, which is about 0.5 metres away at the bottom right and within arm's reach. The baby raises both arms onto the backrest, and a second young child wearing a dark top is revealed about 1 metre away on the left, standing before a chair, facing right toward the highchair, watching the baby, and gripping the tray's front edge with both hands.
depth: The depth image depicts a room corner bordered by a bright wall that is extremely close on the left—about 0.3–0.6 m away in frames 1–4—and relocates to the upper right in frame 5 when the camera wearer turns and travels around the highchair. Farther into the recessed, darker corner, a small black table, router, and curtains lie roughly 1.5–2.2 m ahead and to the right. In the lower foreground, a baby seated in a highchair is below the wearer at an estimated distance of 0.5–0.9 m, within the wearer's arm's reach; in frame 4, the wearer's hands are holding and pushing the highchair back. Frame 5 also shows a second, older child standing on the floor to the highchair's left, approximately 1.0–1.3 m away, close enough to reach the tray and about 0.4 m from the baby. Over frames 1–4, the wearer steps around to the rear of the highchair, causing the baby's head to slip partly beneath the lower image boundary in frame 4 while the corner table draws nearer to around 1.2 m. In frame 5, the wearer pivots clockwise, placing the highchair in the lower right and bringing the standing child into sight on the left. Compared with the dim RGB view, the depth map more clearly conveys the uninterrupted 3D shape of the blank wall, the vertical height difference between the raised highchair seat and the lower floor, and the precise outline of the router antennas atop the dark table. Nevertheless, it appears inaccurate at the bright, sunlit doorway opening on the far right of frame 1, which is shown as pitch-black and seemingly infinitely distant, and it compresses the depth variation across the angled wall surface.
segmentation: Foreground subjects are separated by the segmentation map in just three of the five frames. It combines the baby with the highchair roughly 0.5–0.9 m below and ahead of the camera wearer in frames 1, 3, and 5, while frame 5 includes portions of the standing child on the left at 1.0–1.3 m. In frame 1, the baby—facing toward the wearer's left/back and looking away—and the highchair form one pink mask labelled 'person.' Frame 3 incorrectly assigns a green 'bowl' mask to the highchair structure surrounding the baby, leaving an unsegmented opening where the baby's head and torso are located. In frame 5, several intersecting 'person' masks cover the tray in pink, the baby's arm and the highchair back at the lower right in cyan, and the standing child plus the background chair on the left in brown and yellow-green. The masks track the highchair's movement from the lower left-center in frame 1 to the bottom right in frames 3 and 5, always within the camera wearer's reach. In frame 5, the standing child faces right toward the highchair, keeps both hands on the tray edge, and gazes slightly upward at the wearer. Although frames 3 and 5 usefully emphasize the exterior shape of the highchair's curved tray and backrest, the map supplies almost no spatial information that is difficult to discern from RGB alone. Taken as a whole, the segmentation is very unreliable: frames 2 and 4 contain no detected people or objects, the corner table, router, and curtains are absent in every frame, and the highchair, background chair, and children are badly misclassified and split among overlapping 'person' and 'bowl' regions.
pose: Only three frames receive 2D yellow body skeletons against the pose map's black background. The seated baby is detected in the lower foreground, about 0.6–0.8 m beneath the camera wearer, in frames 2 and 3, while frame 5 detects the standing child on the left at approximately 1.0–1.3 m from the wearer and around 0.4 m from the baby. The baby's head and upper-torso landmarks in frames 2 and 3 indicate that the baby is sitting within the highchair, turned away and toward the wearer's left/upper-left, looking at the backrest instead of the wearer. Their arms are bent and rest within reach of the backrest and tray as the wearer moves counter-clockwise around the chair. In frame 5, detection transfers to the child standing left of the highchair: the skeleton includes the head, torso, and both extended arms reaching ahead and to the right to grasp the tray edge, with the child's head directed rightward and angled slightly upward toward the camera wearer. The map makes the baby's precise head direction—through the eye, nose, and ear landmarks—and shoulder-to-elbow angles easier to interpret under the steep overhead perspective in frames 2–3. It likewise clarifies the standing child's two-handed reach in frame 5, details partly hidden by blur and shadows in RGB. Even so, the pose output is unreliable because it entirely fails to detect the baby in frames 1, 4—when the highchair back and lower frame boundary substantially occlude the baby—and 5. It also misses the wearer's hands contacting the chair in frame 4, misses the wearer's feet in frame 4, and never generates magenta hand skeletons in any frame.
